title: Eyes on the chips: the seaside war between humans and gulls

words.note: seaside 常作定语：a seaside town（海滨小镇）、a seaside holiday（海边度假）。go to the seaside = 去海边玩，英式说法。
words.ctx: Eyes on the chips: the seaside war between humans and gulls

ex.en: We spent a week in a small [[seaside]] town.
ex.zh: 我们在一个海边小镇住了一周。

ex.en: Every August the family goes to the [[seaside]].
ex.zh: 每年八月，一家人都去海边。

cloze.before: Eyes on the chips: the
cloze.after: war between humans and gulls
cloze.szh: 盯紧你的薯条：海边的人鸥大战

words.note: bold 可褒可贬：a bold plan（大胆的计划）；说动物或孩子 bold，常带“胆子大到不客气”的意思。比较级 bolder，最高级 boldest。
words.ctx: Across the world's beach towns, bold seabirds have learned that tourists are an easy meal.

ex.en: The [[bold]] squirrel took a nut right out of my hand.
ex.zh: 那只胆大的松鼠直接从我手里拿走了坚果。

ex.en: It was a [[bold]] decision to quit her job.
ex.zh: 辞掉工作是个大胆的决定。

cloze.before: Across the world's beach towns,
cloze.after: seabirds have learned that tourists are an easy meal.
cloze.szh: 在世界各地的海滩小镇，胆大的海鸟已经摸清了：游客就是送上门的一顿饭。

words.note: 英式 defence，美式 defense。a defence against sth = 抵御……的办法。动词是 defend。
words.ctx: Scientists think they have found a surprisingly simple defence.

ex.en: Sunscreen is your best [[defence]] against sunburn.
ex.zh: 防晒霜是防晒伤最好的办法。

ex.en: The castle walls were the town's main [[defence]].
ex.zh: 城墙是这座城镇主要的防御。

cloze.before: Scientists think they have found a surprisingly simple
cloze.szh: 科学家认为，他们找到了一个简单得出奇的防御办法。

words.note: 同义说法：in an instant、in no time。I'll be back in a flash. = 我马上回来。
words.ctx: It happens in a flash.

ex.en: The cake was gone [[in a flash]].
ex.zh: 蛋糕一眨眼就没了。

ex.en: I'll be back [[in a flash]].
ex.zh: 我马上回来。

cloze.before: It happens in a
cloze.szh: 事情就发生在一眨眼之间。

words.note: un- 表示相反的动作：wrap（包）→ unwrap（拆开）；lock → unlock；pack → unpack。
words.ctx: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall, unwraps a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull swoops down and makes off with the biggest piece.

ex.en: The kids [[unwrapped]] their presents in seconds.
ex.zh: 孩子们几秒钟就把礼物拆开了。

ex.en: She [[unwraps]] a sandwich at her desk every day at noon.
ex.zh: 她每天中午在办公桌前拆开一个三明治。

cloze.before: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall,
cloze.after: a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull swoops down and makes off with the biggest piece.
cloze.szh: 一家人在康沃尔的海堤上坐下，拆开一包用纸裹着的炸鱼薯条，还没等谁咬上一口，一只银鸥就俯冲下来，叼走了最大的那块。

words.note: swoop 指鸟从空中猛扑下来，也可以比喻突然行动：Police swooped on the house.（警察突袭了那栋房子。）
words.ctx: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall, unwraps a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull swoops down and makes off with the biggest piece.

ex.en: An owl [[swooped down]] and caught a mouse.
ex.zh: 一只猫头鹰俯冲下来抓住了一只老鼠。

ex.en: Watch the eagle [[swoop down]] towards the river.
ex.zh: 看那只鹰朝河面俯冲下去。

cloze.before: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall, unwraps a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull
cloze.after: down and makes off with the biggest piece.
cloze.szh: 一家人在康沃尔的海堤上坐下，拆开一包用纸裹着的炸鱼薯条，还没等谁咬上一口，一只银鸥就俯冲下来，叼走了最大的那块。

words.note: make off = 匆匆逃走；make off with sth = 带着（偷来的）东西跑掉。比 steal 更口语，更有画面感。
words.ctx: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall, unwraps a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull swoops down and makes off with the biggest piece.

ex.en: A thief [[made off with]] her handbag.
ex.zh: 一个小偷抢了她的手提包就跑了。

ex.en: The dog [[made off with]] a sausage from the barbecue.
ex.zh: 狗从烧烤架上叼了一根香肠就跑。

cloze.before: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall, unwraps a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull swoops down and
cloze.after: off with the biggest piece.
cloze.szh: 一家人在康沃尔的海堤上坐下，拆开一包用纸裹着的炸鱼薯条，还没等谁咬上一口，一只银鸥就俯冲下来，叼走了最大的那块。

words.note: shriek 比 scream 更尖、更短。shriek with laughter = 笑得尖叫。也可作名词：a shriek of delight。
words.ctx: The children shriek, the parents shout, and the bird retreats to a rooftop to enjoy its prize.

ex.en: The kids [[shrieked]] when the cold wave hit them.
ex.zh: 冰冷的浪打过来，孩子们尖叫起来。

ex.en: She [[shrieked]] with laughter at the joke.
ex.zh: 她听到笑话笑得尖叫。

cloze.before: The children
cloze.after: , the parents shout, and the bird retreats to a rooftop to enjoy its prize.
cloze.szh: 孩子们尖叫，大人们大喊，那只鸟则退到屋顶上享用它的战利品。

words.note: retreat 原是军事用语“撤退”，也常用于日常：retreat to one's room（躲回自己房间）。名词 a retreat 还可以指静修的地方。
words.ctx: The children shriek, the parents shout, and the bird retreats to a rooftop to enjoy its prize.

ex.en: The cat [[retreated]] under the bed when the guests arrived.
ex.zh: 客人一来，猫就躲到床底下去了。

ex.en: After lunch he [[retreats]] to his study to read.
ex.zh: 午饭后他总是躲进书房看书。

cloze.before: The children shriek, the parents shout, and the bird
cloze.after: to a rooftop to enjoy its prize.
cloze.szh: 孩子们尖叫，大人们大喊，那只鸟则退到屋顶上享用它的战利品。

words.note: play out 指事情一步步展开、发生，常用于场景、局面：We'll see how things play out.（看事情怎么发展吧。）
words.ctx: Similar scenes play out every summer from Brighton to Sydney to Cape Town.

ex.en: The same argument [[plays out]] in our house every Sunday.
ex.zh: 每个星期天，我们家都会上演同样的争吵。

ex.en: Let's wait and see how things [[play out]].
ex.zh: 我们等着看事情怎么发展吧。

cloze.before: Similar scenes
cloze.after: out every summer from Brighton to Sydney to Cape Town.
cloze.szh: 从布莱顿到悉尼再到开普敦，每年夏天都在上演类似的场面。

words.note: 英式口语，常说小孩或宠物，不算很重的批评，带一点好笑：a cheeky grin（调皮的笑）。
words.ctx: Gulls were not always this cheeky.

ex.en: Don't be [[cheeky]] to your teacher.
ex.zh: 别对老师没大没小的。

ex.en: He gave me a [[cheeky]] grin and took the last biscuit.
ex.zh: 他冲我调皮一笑，拿走了最后一块饼干。

cloze.before: Gulls were not always this
cloze.szh: 海鸥并不是一直都这么厚脸皮。

words.note: scavenger 指食腐动物，比如秃鹫、鬣狗。人也可以 scavenge for sth：在旧物里翻找能用的东西。
words.ctx: For most of their history they fed at sea, scavenging behind fishing boats and picking through the shoreline.

ex.en: Foxes [[scavenge]] for scraps in the bins at night.
ex.zh: 狐狸夜里在垃圾桶里翻找残羹剩饭。

ex.en: We [[scavenged]] wood from the beach for the fire.
ex.zh: 我们在海滩上捡木头生火。

cloze.before: For most of their history they fed at sea,
cloze.after: behind fishing boats and picking through the shoreline.
cloze.szh: 在漫长的历史中，它们大多在海上觅食，跟在渔船后面捡食，在海岸边翻找吃的。

words.note: pick through 强调一件件地挑、翻：pick through the rubbish / the evidence。
words.ctx: For most of their history they fed at sea, scavenging behind fishing boats and picking through the shoreline.

ex.en: She [[picked through]] the box of old photos.
ex.zh: 她把那箱旧照片翻了个遍。

ex.en: Birds were [[picking through]] the rubbish.
ex.zh: 几只鸟在垃圾里翻找。

cloze.before: For most of their history they fed at sea, scavenging behind fishing boats and
cloze.after: through the shoreline.
cloze.szh: 在漫长的历史中，它们大多在海上觅食，跟在渔船后面捡食，在海岸边翻找吃的。

words.note: dwindle 强调慢慢变少、越来越小：dwindling numbers（越来越少的数量）。近义 shrink，但 dwindle 更强调“所剩无几”。
words.ctx: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.

ex.en: Our savings [[dwindled]] during the long holiday.
ex.zh: 长假期间我们的积蓄越来越少。

ex.en: The crowd [[dwindled]] as the rain got heavier.
ex.zh: 雨越下越大，人群渐渐散去。

cloze.before: But as fish stocks
cloze.after: and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.
cloze.szh: 可随着鱼类资源越来越少，镇上到处是垃圾、垃圾桶和露天吃饭的人，许多海鸥搬到了内陆，而且适应得快得惊人。

words.note: fill up 是装满；fill up with sth 说明用什么装满。也说加满油：fill up the car。
words.ctx: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.

ex.en: The room soon [[filled up with]] smoke.
ex.zh: 房间里很快烟雾弥漫。

ex.en: Her eyes [[filled up with]] tears.
ex.zh: 她的眼里噙满了泪水。

cloze.before: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns
cloze.after: up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.
cloze.szh: 可随着鱼类资源越来越少，镇上到处是垃圾、垃圾桶和露天吃饭的人，许多海鸥搬到了内陆，而且适应得快得惊人。

words.note: inland 可作副词（move inland）也可作形容词（an inland city，内陆城市）。反义是 coastal（沿海的）。
words.ctx: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.

ex.en: The storm moved [[inland]] overnight.
ex.zh: 风暴一夜之间移到了内陆。

ex.en: They live in a small [[inland]] village.
ex.zh: 他们住在一个内陆小村子里。

cloze.before: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved
cloze.after: and adapted with remarkable speed.
cloze.szh: 可随着鱼类资源越来越少，镇上到处是垃圾、垃圾桶和露天吃饭的人，许多海鸥搬到了内陆，而且适应得快得惊人。

words.note: adapt to sth：适应……。adapt 也可以表示“改编”：adapt a novel for the screen。形容词 adaptable = 适应力强的。
words.ctx: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.

ex.en: Children [[adapt]] quickly to a new school.
ex.zh: 孩子们很快就能适应新学校。

ex.en: The company [[adapted]] to online sales.
ex.zh: 公司转向了网上销售。

cloze.before: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and
cloze.after: with remarkable speed.
cloze.szh: 可随着鱼类资源越来越少，镇上到处是垃圾、垃圾桶和露天吃饭的人，许多海鸥搬到了内陆，而且适应得快得惊人。

words.note: come by sth = 得到、弄到。常用 hard to come by（难得、不好找）：Good jobs are hard to come by.
words.ctx: A city gull can live for 20 years, remembers where food is easy to come by, and learns by watching other gulls get away with theft.

ex.en: Cheap flats are hard to [[come by]] in London.
ex.zh: 在伦敦很难找到便宜的公寓。

ex.en: In summer, fresh fruit is [[easy to come by]].
ex.zh: 夏天新鲜水果很容易买到。

cloze.before: A city gull can live for 20 years, remembers where food is easy to
cloze.after: by, and learns by watching other gulls get away with theft.
cloze.szh: 一只城市海鸥能活二十年，记得哪里容易找到吃的，还会看着别的海鸥偷了东西没事，跟着学。

words.note: get away with sth：做了错事却逃过惩罚。You won't get away with this! = 你逃不掉的！
words.ctx: A city gull can live for 20 years, remembers where food is easy to come by, and learns by watching other gulls get away with theft.

ex.en: He cheated and [[got away with]] it.
ex.zh: 他作弊了，却什么事也没有。

ex.en: You can't [[get away with]] being late every day.
ex.zh: 你不能天天迟到还不受处罚。

cloze.before: A city gull can live for 20 years, remembers where food is easy to come by, and learns by watching other gulls get
cloze.after: with theft.
cloze.szh: 一只城市海鸥能活二十年，记得哪里容易找到吃的，还会看着别的海鸥偷了东西没事，跟着学。

words.note: 注意 wits' 的撇号在 s 后面（复数所有格）。常说 I'm at my wits' end. = 我真是没辙了。
words.ctx: Residents are at their wits' end.

ex.en: The new parents were [[at their wits' end]] after a week without sleep.
ex.zh: 一周没睡好，这对新手父母已经束手无策了。

ex.en: I'm [[at my wits' end]] with this printer.
ex.zh: 这台打印机真让我没辙了。

cloze.before: Residents are at their wits'
cloze.szh: 居民们已经无计可施了。

words.zh: 从 A 到 B 什么都……
words.note: 用来表示种类繁多：The shop sells everything from socks to sofas.
words.ctx: Councils have tried everything from spiked roofs and fake owls to fines for anyone caught feeding the birds.

ex.en: The market sells [[everything from]] fish to phone cases.
ex.zh: 这个市场什么都卖，从鱼到手机壳。

ex.en: We talked about [[everything from]] football to philosophy.
ex.zh: 我们什么都聊，从足球到哲学。

cloze.before: Councils have tried
cloze.after: from spiked roofs and fake owls to fines for anyone caught feeding the birds.
cloze.szh: 地方政府什么办法都试过：从在屋顶装尖刺、摆假猫头鹰，到对被抓到喂鸟的人罚款。

words.note: fine 作名词是“罚款”，作动词是“处以罚款”：He was fined £100. 别和形容词 fine（好的）弄混。
words.ctx: Councils have tried everything from spiked roofs and fake owls to fines for anyone caught feeding the birds.

ex.en: She got a parking [[fine]] outside the hospital.
ex.zh: 她在医院外面吃了一张停车罚单。

ex.en: Drivers are [[fined]] for using their phones.
ex.zh: 司机开车用手机会被罚款。

cloze.before: Councils have tried everything from spiked roofs and fake owls to
cloze.after: for anyone caught feeding the birds.
cloze.szh: 地方政府什么办法都试过：从在屋顶装尖刺、摆假猫头鹰，到对被抓到喂鸟的人罚款。

words.note: scare sb/sth off 或 scare off sb/sth。也说 scare away。比喻用法：High prices scared buyers off.（高价把买家吓跑了。）
words.ctx: Some towns have hired falconers, whose hawks patrol the beach to scare gulls off.

ex.en: The dog barked and [[scared]] the burglars off.
ex.zh: 狗一叫，把小偷吓跑了。

ex.en: High prices may [[scare off]] tourists.
ex.zh: 高价可能会把游客吓跑。

cloze.before: Some towns have hired falconers, whose hawks patrol the beach to
cloze.after: gulls off.
cloze.szh: 有些镇雇了驯鹰人，让他们的鹰在海滩上巡逻，把海鸥吓跑。

words.note: 两个常用意思：一是“领会、反应过来”（The kids caught on fast.）；二是“流行起来”（The fashion never caught on.）。
words.ctx: Most of these measures work for a while; then the gulls catch on and come back.

ex.en: It took me a while to [[catch on]] to the joke.
ex.zh: 我过了一会儿才明白这个笑话。

ex.en: The new app never really [[caught on]].
ex.zh: 这个新应用一直没真正流行起来。

cloze.before: Most of these measures work for a while; then the gulls
cloze.after: on and come back.
cloze.szh: 这些办法大多能管用一阵子，然后海鸥就看穿了，又回来了。

words.note: come up with an idea / a plan / an answer / an excuse。比 think of 更强调“想出来了”。
words.ctx: Researchers studying gull behaviour have come up with a cheaper idea: stare them down.

ex.en: She [[came up with]] a clever name for the shop.
ex.zh: 她给店想了个巧妙的名字。

ex.en: We need to [[come up with]] a plan by Friday.
ex.zh: 我们得在周五前想出个计划。

cloze.before: Researchers studying gull behaviour have
cloze.after: up with a cheaper idea: stare them down.
cloze.szh: 研究海鸥行为的研究人员想出了一个更省钱的办法：瞪着它们，直到它们退缩。

words.note: stare at sb = 盯着某人看；stare sb down 更进一步，盯到对方先移开目光或退缩。
words.ctx: Researchers studying gull behaviour have come up with a cheaper idea: stare them down.

ex.en: The cat [[stared]] the dog down.
ex.zh: 猫一直瞪着狗，直到狗退缩。

ex.en: Don't try to [[stare down]] an angry bull.
ex.zh: 别跟一头发怒的公牛对视。

cloze.before: Researchers studying gull behaviour have come up with a cheaper idea:
cloze.after: them down.
cloze.szh: 研究海鸥行为的研究人员想出了一个更省钱的办法：瞪着它们，直到它们退缩。

words.note: approach 作动词时直接跟宾语：approach the door（不说 approach to）。也可以指“着手处理”：approach a problem。
words.ctx: In one experiment, scientists placed a bag of chips on the ground and watched how long passing gulls took to approach it.

ex.en: A stranger [[approached]] me in the street.
ex.zh: 街上有个陌生人朝我走过来。

ex.en: Winter is [[approaching]] fast.
ex.zh: 冬天很快就要到了。

cloze.before: In one experiment, scientists placed a bag of chips on the ground and watched how long passing gulls took to
cloze.after: it.
cloze.szh: 在一项实验里，科学家把一袋薯条放在地上，观察路过的海鸥要过多久才会靠近。

words.note: hesitate to do sth：迟疑着不做。礼貌用语 Don't hesitate to ask. = 有问题尽管问。名词 hesitation。
words.ctx: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up altogether.

ex.en: She [[hesitated]] before opening the letter.
ex.zh: 她犹豫了一下才拆开信。

ex.en: Don't [[hesitate]] to call me if you need help.
ex.zh: 需要帮忙就尽管给我打电话。

cloze.before: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it
cloze.after: far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up altogether.
cloze.szh: 如果人一直盯着鸟看，它犹豫的时间比人把目光移开时长得多，很多干脆放弃了。

words.note: give up (doing) sth：放弃、戒掉：give up smoking。give up on sb = 对某人不抱希望。
words.ctx: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up altogether.

ex.en: He [[gave up]] after three tries.
ex.zh: 他试了三次就放弃了。

ex.en: Never [[give up]] on your dreams.
ex.zh: 永远不要放弃你的梦想。

cloze.before: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many
cloze.after: up altogether.
cloze.szh: 如果人一直盯着鸟看，它犹豫的时间比人把目光移开时长得多，很多干脆放弃了。

words.note: altogether 有两个意思：一是“完全”（stop altogether），二是“总共”（£50 altogether）。注意和 all together（大家一起）区分。
words.ctx: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up altogether.

ex.en: The noise stopped [[altogether]].
ex.zh: 噪音完全停了。

ex.en: We might cancel the trip [[altogether]].
ex.zh: 我们可能会彻底取消这次旅行。

cloze.before: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up
cloze.szh: 如果人一直盯着鸟看，它犹豫的时间比人把目光移开时长得多，很多干脆放弃了。

words.note: wary 指小心提防，比 careful 多一层“不信任”：be wary of strangers。名词形式 wariness。
words.ctx: Gulls, it seems, are wary of being watched, perhaps because a staring animal is more likely to fight back.

ex.en: Cats are [[wary of]] strangers.
ex.zh: 猫对陌生人有戒心。

ex.en: Be [[wary of]] offers that sound too good to be true.
ex.zh: 好得不像真的优惠，要多留个心眼。

cloze.before: Gulls, it seems, are
cloze.after: of being watched, perhaps because a staring animal is more likely to fight back.
cloze.szh: 看来，海鸥不喜欢被人盯着，也许是因为一个瞪着你的动物更可能会反击。

words.note: fight back 也可以指“忍住（眼泪等）”：fight back tears。
words.ctx: Gulls, it seems, are wary of being watched, perhaps because a staring animal is more likely to fight back.

ex.en: When the bully pushed him, he [[fought back]].
ex.zh: 那个恶霸推他时，他还手了。

ex.en: She [[fought back]] tears during the speech.
ex.zh: 她演讲时强忍着眼泪。

cloze.after: back.
cloze.szh: 看来，海鸥不喜欢被人盯着，也许是因为一个瞪着你的动物更可能会反击。

words.zh: 有个隐藏的问题、有个“但是”
words.note: catch 作名词指暗藏的问题或代价。常见问法：What's the catch?（有什么猫腻？）
words.ctx: There is a catch, of course.

ex.en: The flight is very cheap, but [[there is a catch]]: no luggage.
ex.zh: 机票很便宜，但有个问题：不含行李。

ex.en: Free pizza for a year? [[What's the catch]]?
ex.zh: 一年免费披萨？有什么猫腻？

cloze.before: There is a
cloze.after: , of course.
cloze.szh: 当然，这里面也有个问题。

words.note: 反义 the majority of（大多数）。in the minority = 属于少数。
words.ctx: Only a minority of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest barely paused before grabbing it.

ex.en: Only [[a minority of]] students walk to school.
ex.zh: 只有少数学生走路上学。

ex.en: [[A minority of]] drivers cause most accidents.
ex.zh: 大多数事故是少数司机造成的。

cloze.before: Only a
cloze.after: of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest barely paused before grabbing it.
cloze.szh: 只有少数海鸥敢靠近食物，而胆子最大的那几只几乎不停顿就抢走了。

words.note: dare 可以接 to do 或直接接动词原形：He didn't dare (to) look.。I dare you to ... = 我赌你不敢……。
words.ctx: Only a minority of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest barely paused before grabbing it.

ex.en: Nobody [[dared to]] tell the boss.
ex.zh: 没人敢告诉老板。

ex.en: I didn't [[dare]] look down from the bridge.
ex.zh: 我不敢从桥上往下看。

cloze.before: Only a minority of the gulls

cloze.szh: 只有少数海鸥敢靠近食物，而胆子最大的那几只几乎不停顿就抢走了。

words.note: barely 带否定意味：I barely slept. = 我几乎没睡。也表示“刚刚够”：She barely caught the train.（她差点没赶上火车。）
words.ctx: Only a minority of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest barely paused before grabbing it.

ex.en: I could [[barely]] hear him over the music.
ex.zh: 音乐太吵，我几乎听不见他说话。

ex.en: We [[barely]] made it to the airport on time.
ex.zh: 我们差一点就没按时赶到机场。

cloze.before: Only a minority of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest
cloze.after: paused before grabbing it.
cloze.szh: 只有少数海鸥敢靠近食物，而胆子最大的那几只几乎不停顿就抢走了。

words.note: keep an eye on sb/sth：照看、留心。Can you keep an eye on my bag? = 能帮我看一下包吗？
words.ctx: And it is hard to keep an eye on a gull while also eating, chatting and keeping track of small children.

ex.en: Can you [[keep an eye on]] my bag for a minute?
ex.zh: 能帮我看一下包吗？

ex.en: The teacher [[kept an eye on]] the quiet boy at the back.
ex.zh: 老师一直留意着后排那个安静的男孩。

cloze.before: And it is hard to keep an
cloze.after: on a gull while also eating, chatting and keeping track of small children.
cloze.szh: 而且一边吃东西、聊天、看着小孩，一边还要盯住一只海鸥，实在不容易。

words.note: keep track of sth：随时了解、记录。反义 lose track of：搞不清、忘了。lose track of time = 忘了时间。
words.ctx: And it is hard to keep an eye on a gull while also eating, chatting and keeping track of small children.

ex.en: I use an app to [[keep track of]] my spending.
ex.zh: 我用一个应用记录开支。

ex.en: We [[lost track of]] time and missed the bus.
ex.zh: 我们忘了时间，错过了公交车。

cloze.before: And it is hard to keep an eye on a gull while also eating, chatting and keeping
cloze.after: of small children.
cloze.szh: 而且一边吃东西、聊天、看着小孩，一边还要盯住一只海鸥，实在不容易。

words.note: hint 作名词是“暗示、提示”：give sb a hint。hint at sth = 间接地提到、暗示。
words.ctx: Still, the finding hints at something that frustrated towns often miss.

ex.en: He [[hinted at]] a big announcement next week.
ex.zh: 他暗示下周会有重大消息。

ex.en: The dark clouds [[hint at]] a storm.
ex.zh: 乌云预示着暴风雨。

cloze.before: Still, the finding
cloze.after: at something that frustrated towns often miss.
cloze.szh: 不过，这个发现指出了一点，焦头烂额的小镇常常忽略。

words.zh: 投机者、善于抓机会的人
words.note: opportunist 常带贬义，指只顾自己利益抓机会的人；说动物时就是“见机行事”。形容词 opportunistic。
words.ctx: Gulls are not villains; they are opportunists doing what any sensible animal would do when food is left lying around.

ex.en: Foxes are clever [[opportunists]] that eat almost anything.
ex.zh: 狐狸是聪明的机会主义者，几乎什么都吃。

ex.en: Some politicians are pure [[opportunists]].
ex.zh: 有些政客完全是投机分子。

cloze.before: Gulls are not villains; they are
cloze.after: doing what any sensible animal would do when food is left lying around.
cloze.szh: 海鸥并不是坏蛋；它们只是投机者，吃的东西随便放着的时候，任何聪明的动物都会这么做。

words.note: leave sth lying around = 把东西乱放。也可以说人“闲躺着”：lie around all day。
words.ctx: Gulls are not villains; they are opportunists doing what any sensible animal would do when food is left lying around.

ex.en: Don't leave your keys [[lying around]].
ex.zh: 别把钥匙到处乱放。

ex.en: There were toys [[lying around]] everywhere.
ex.zh: 到处都乱扔着玩具。

cloze.after: around.
cloze.szh: 海鸥并不是坏蛋；它们只是投机者，吃的东西随便放着的时候，任何聪明的动物都会这么做。

words.note: in decline = declining。也说 go into decline（开始衰落）、a decline in sth（……的下降）。
words.ctx: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.

ex.en: The old industry has been [[in decline]] for years.
ex.zh: 那个老行业已经衰落多年了。

ex.en: Bee numbers are [[in decline]] in many countries.
ex.zh: 许多国家的蜜蜂数量在减少。

cloze.before: Many species are in

cloze.szh: 许多种类的海鸥在海上数量正在减少，而它们城里的“亲戚”却过得很好，所以很难找到理由去捕杀它们。

words.note: even as 引出同时发生、方向相反的事：Prices rose even as wages fell.（工资下降的同时物价却在上涨。）
words.ctx: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.

ex.en: The town grew quieter [[even as]] the city boomed.
ex.zh: 城市繁荣起来的同时，小镇却越来越冷清。

ex.en: He kept smiling [[even as]] he lost the game.
ex.zh: 就在输掉比赛的时候，他还一直在笑。

words.note: thrive 指在某种环境下长得好、过得好：Plants thrive in sunlight. thrive on sth = 靠……茁壮成长。形容词 thriving。
words.ctx: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.

ex.en: Tomatoes [[thrive]] in warm weather.
ex.zh: 番茄在暖和的天气里长得好。

ex.en: Some people [[thrive]] under pressure.
ex.zh: 有些人越有压力越出色。

words.zh: 很难说得过去、很难找到理由
words.note: justify：证明……有道理、为……辩护。名词 justification。The end justifies the means. = 为达目的不择手段。
words.ctx: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.

ex.en: Such a high price is [[hard to justify]].
ex.zh: 这么高的价格很难说得过去。

ex.en: How can you [[justify]] spending so much?
ex.zh: 你怎么解释花这么多钱是合理的？

words.note: 常用来引出最后的办法，带点幽默：When all else fails, read the instructions.（实在不行，就看说明书吧。）
words.ctx: The best defence may simply be to eat indoors, keep bins closed and, when all else fails, look the bird in the eye.

ex.en: [[When all else fails]], turn it off and on again.
ex.zh: 实在不行，就关了再开一次。

ex.en: [[If all else fails]], we can take a taxi.
ex.zh: 要是其他办法都不行，我们就打车。

m: look the bird in the eye

ex.zh: 他不敢正眼看我。

ex.en: She [[looked him in the eye]] and said no.
ex.zh: 她直视着他的眼睛说了不。
